title: Review: silent e + bossy r
parentNote: Nothing new today, but this is the hardest review so far, because two patterns that both live on a vowel finally turn up in the same lesson. A quiet e on the end makes the vowel say its name — cap becomes cape. An r after the vowel takes the sound over instead — cap becomes car. Today your child has to look at the whole word before deciding, which is the real skill and the reason for all the cap / cape / car sets below. If they guess wrong, don't say no; say "look at the end of the word" and let them try again. There are two stories, so stop after the first if the going is slow — finishing while it is still going well beats getting to the bottom of the list.

activities.prompt: Three ways to use an a. One has a quiet e waiting, one has an r taking over, and one is on its own.
Now the same three with an o. Listen for the r.
And with a u. The quiet e one is the only one where the u says its own name.
Nothing new today. This one has the quiet e, so the n and the e go together.
The tricky one. A bossy r AND a quiet e in the same short word, and they both do their job.
Same three letters at the front. The end of the word decides all of it.
Quiet e, bossy r, or nothing at all? Listen to the middle.
One more set. Say all three out loud first, then listen.

activities.text: Bart did carve a grin on a turnip and did set it in the dark barn.
Are the spade and the fork in the shed or under the stone?
Fern did hide the cake under a birch, and her big dog did spot it.

activities.title: The hornet in the shed
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Bart went in the shed for a spade.
Up in the corner is a nest, and in the nest is a hornet.
The hornet is cross, and it came at Bart fast.
Bart ran and did shut the shed up.
Then Fern came with a big glass jar and a card.
Fern did creep in and did pop the jar on the hornet.
Then Fern did slide the card under the jar.
Fern went up the path and did set the hornet free in the ferns.
The hornet did not sting her. It just went home.
Bart did grin at Fern. Fern is brave, and Bart is still hid in the barn!

activities.title: The note in the birch
activities.prompt: One more. This one ends with a joke.
lines: Meg made a den under a big birch.
Meg did hide a note in a hole in the birch.
The note is for her sister Fern.
But a bird did spot the note, and the bird did take it.
Fern did hunt under the birch and did not spot a note.
Then Fern did spot a nest up in the birch.
In the nest is a bird, three eggs and the note, in bits.
Fern did grin. The note is a nest, and the eggs are snug.
Meg did make a note. The bird did make a bed!
